title: Lesson 33 - Standard and Custom Topics and Actions: The Agentforce Building Blocks
description: Given a scenario, select and configure standard topics, custom topics, standard Agent actions, and custom Agent actions.

questions.question: A team wants the agent to handle order status and returns reliably, and the standard topics are too broad. What does Salesforce recommend?
options: Replace the broad standard topic with purpose-built custom topics that have narrow classification descriptions
Keep one broad standard topic and add more actions to it
Put the routing rules in topic instructions
Remove the classification description so the agent infers the job
questions.explanation: Salesforce states that narrow, clearly described topics classify more reliably than a catch-all, so specific custom topics beat a broad standard topic for this need.

questions.question: Where should a business rule that must always behave the same way live?
options: In the action's own Flow or Apex logic
questions.explanation: Topic and action instructions are non-deterministic, so deterministic or sensitive rules belong inside the action's Flow or Apex, where they always execute the same way.

questions.question: Two admins can both open an agent, but only one can run one of its custom actions. What explains this?
options: Custom actions are randomly assigned per user
The action is hidden until the agent is activated
A custom action inherits the access of the Flow, Apex class, or prompt template it references
Standard actions are required before custom actions run
questions.explanation: Access to a custom action depends on the asset behind it, so permission to the referenced Flow or Apex determines who can invoke the action.
